The driver is the long end: 10Y hit 5.361% and 30Y 5.73%, both highest since 2002, then a strong $39B 10-year auction (~13:00) turned yields and stocks off the lows; 10Y closed 5.276% (WSJ/Tullett; Barron's ticker 5.295). Thursday's structure: 08:30 claims sets the open, then the market waits for the 13:00 $22B 30-year reopening - the first long-end auction at a 2002-high yield one day after a strong 10-year. Expect chop inside 773.61-779.09 until 13:00, then a directional move keyed to the auction tail/stop-through. DAY-2 BIAS for the yield-spike-then-reversal: a reversal built on one auction holds only if the second auction confirms; a strong 30-year (stop-through, high indirects) = continuation of the Wed-afternoon relief -> SPY reclaims 779.09, rate-sensitives (banks, small caps, REITs, miners) squeeze; a tailed 30-year = the reversal was a one-day event -> 30Y back toward 5.73%, SPY loses 773.61 and the AI/semis fade (NVDA under Tue low 238.93) resumes. Equity-only pattern (not web-verified, from memory): a -0.2% first down day after a 4-day run to records in a 50/200-day uptrend more often retests the high than continues down - but Wed's breadth says the retest is mega-cap-only.
